concepts.title: Fidelity and Adaptation: The Messenger Model
concepts.description: the extension corpus's best-chosen analogy, absolute fidelity to the transmission plus adaptation for reception, and the two requirements pulling against each other. **The Aṅka supplies the missing third variable**: Hanuman deliberately declined Sanskrit before addressing Sītā because it would read as another of Rāvaṇa's deceptions, choosing the vernacular of Kosala — Vālmīki 5.33.14, *mānuṣaṃ vākyam*, Govindarāja's gloss — the best Sanskritist in the epic using plain speech at the moment competence would have been fatal. Plus **the courier's category as a delegation test**: sort work by whether partial failure yields a partial result, which is a property of the task rather than of the delegate. ⚠ The same source document carries fabricated performance figures, treated on the page

concepts.title: The Envoy Sent Without Instructions
concepts.description: ***niśṛṣṭārtha dūta***, Sanskrit dramatic theory's category for an envoy trusted to act on his own judgment toward a goal his master never spelled out, evidenced not by the Laṅkā mission but by **Ṛṣyamūka**, where Hanuman is sent only to identify two strangers and brokers the alliance the rest of the epic runs on. Against **the opposite doctrine printed two pages earlier** — word for word, adding nothing and softening nothing. ⚑ **The tradition supplies its own limit**: the Trikūṭa pause, where the same figure exercises discretion by declining to act, reasoning that *envoys who trust their own cleverness ruin missions* — a disposition rather than a rule, because discretion constrained from outside is just a brief again. **Which kind you need is decided by whether the sender can specify the goal**, not by assessing the delegate

concepts.title: The Study of Fifty Practitioners
concepts.description: the corpus's Evidence document reports *"following 50 practitioners through complete implementation cycle"* with *"80% show sustained income growth, 90% report higher work satisfaction"*, plus 2–3× pricing, acquisition costs down 60–80% and **5–10× annual income within 24 months**. ⚑ **The same corpus's SWOT states real revenue of $465 a year, four paid subscribers, and concedes *"the revenue math doesn't work yet."*** One corpus, two documents, irreconcilable. **The fabrication is not confined to the Evidence document** — the Problem Definition carries unattributed isolation statistics (*"55% of freelancers report depression compared to 30% of office workers"*), and real researchers (Deci & Ryan, Ariely, Pink; MIT CCI, Stanford HAI) are attached to claims with no specific paper, which is CLAUDE.md's CONSENSUS MISREPRESENTATION flag exactly. **The arithmetic fails internally**: *"3 validated products per week (72 annually)"* — 3 × 52 = 156. And the *failure* cases are invented too, which is a strange act worth its own section. **The SWOT is the interesting document**, because it proves the capacity for candour was present and was not spent

concepts.title: The Anonymity Test
concepts.description: *"Would you pursue the same level of strategic excellence if no one ever knew about your service?"* — one of four Authenticity Tests in the corpus's most disciplined document. **Three properties almost nothing else in the corpus has**: first-person, able to come back no, and **anti-correlated with the failure mode** — somebody sliding into self-promotion answers it worse over time. It does not weigh motives; it **varies the one thing that distinguishes service from reputation-seeking** and asks what survives. ⚑ **The corpus owns the cure and never administers it**: the archetypal cluster's three-year progression gates run entirely on other people's regard, and its only named failure mode produces exactly those reports. Third instance of one shape in this build — *the corpus produces the correction and files it where the problem is not* — and the mechanism is that separate documents never come into contact, so **a corpus cannot audit itself.** The Measurement Framework splits the same way: countable first-person quantitative indicators beside a self-rated *"Dharmic Alignment Scale (1–10 daily)"*. Rāmsukhdās converges on the same shape from 1975 — *has the unglamorous serving continued undiminished?*

concepts.title: Constraints That Widen the Option Set
concepts.description: *"Ethical boundaries paradoxically increase strategic options"*, the corpus's most repeated claim, stated four times **with no worked instance in sixteen documents**. The mechanism is costly signalling: a constraint you are *known* to hold changes what others do, and the credibility it buys cannot be purchased at any price precisely because it was expensive. ⚑ **The volume supplies three instances the corpus never cites** — Rāma's *abhaya* vow (Vālmīki 6.18.33), which removes the king's discretion and buys Vibhīṣaṇa; the envoy's limits, which make the immunity claim usable; and the Dvārakā prohibition on *māraṇa*/*mohana*. **The correct form of the claim is harder than the corpus's**: a public constraint does not increase your options, it changes the population that approaches you, and you pay in the cases where it was wrong. ⚠ **Only the checkable prohibitions can do the signalling work** — the corpus's positive constraints (*serve genuine problems before self-interest*) cannot be breached and therefore cannot be signalled — and the Dharmic Moat, Humble Giant Positioning and the Anonymity Test cannot all be followed at once, since a moat of refusals requires the record to be legible

concepts.title: The Conflict-Resolution Hierarchy
concepts.description: the framework's twenty foundational axioms come with something almost no values framework has: **a stated order of precedence.** *Service orientation → long-term sustainability → integration opportunity → cultural contribution*, restated as Tool 14. **A list of values is not a decision procedure**; it is a vocabulary for justifying decisions already made, because with four terms available there is always one the chosen action served. A strict order binds and can return an answer you dislike. ⚑ **Run it on the corpus's own conflicts and it splits**: it resolves the fabricated fifty-practitioner study decisively at term one — and never ran — while the memetic-engineering material **passes at every term**, because no term examines the third party and *service orientation* asks about the operator's aim rather than the act. ⚠ **Twenty axioms, four ranked**: sixteen have no precedence relation to anything, including *dharmic constraints enable freedom*, which this build has already shown colliding with two other commitments in the same corpus. The framework's best structural achievement is a sample rather than a system, and finishing it needs no new sources — only deciding

concepts.title: The Paradigms That State Their Own Drawbacks
concepts.description: five paradigms (Rakshasa Reversal, Kaliyuga Chaos Surfing, Satsang Network Effect, Pratyāhāra Attention Warfare, Bhakti Revenue Alchemy), **each carrying an unforced *Potential Drawbacks* block** in a document that calls itself revolutionary, with no reviewer, no editor and no audience demanding it. **Two kinds of candour, and this is the rarer**: the SWOT's $465 is confessional and dates; a stated limit is architectural and survives into every future use. ⚑ **Rigour tracks the document's register, not the author's competence** — fourth instance in this build — and the register is identifiable in advance from the title, which makes the rule operational: *Core Principles* and *Strategic Devotion* are reliable, *Evidence & Case Studies* is the least reliable file in the corpus. ⚠ A drawbacks block is a rigour instrument, not an ethics instrument: it cannot reach *Pratyāhāra Attention Warfare*, which keeps a term whose whole content is reflexive and reverses its direction. ⚠ **Five paradigms and no instances** — across sixteen documents the only concrete cases are fabricated or borrowed from Marcus Aurelius, Musashi, Franklin, Douglass, Tubman and Perkins

concepts.title: The Sundarkāṇḍa Sprint
concepts.description: a 7/14/7/7-day work cycle in four phases — **Scout · Infiltrate · Extract Intelligence · Report Back** — mapped onto the Laṅkā mission, and the only construct in the cluster that borrows a narrative's *sequence* rather than its imagery. **Three calls are correct to the text**: the objective really is intelligence rather than rescue, the return-and-report really is the terminus, and the proportions track the book. ⚑ **The four phases omit the burning of Laṅkā and the audience with Rāvaṇa** — everything the mission is remembered for, and everything decided by judgment rather than by the brief. The volume reads the same mission for its **decision structure** and gets the courier's category and the Trikūṭa pause; *a story's phases are its least informative layer, because phases are what any competent plan would have contained*. Repair: a fifth phase between infiltration and extraction, asking *has what I found changed what this is for?* ⚠ And a mission that happened once has no cadence — no memory phase, no rest phase, and an urgency that does not match a repeating thirty-five-day cycle

concepts.title: The Rāma Test and the Decision Filters
concepts.description: *"Does this serve my audience's dharma or just my ego/profit?"*, beside the Dharmic Decision Matrix and four Hanumanic Business Metrics (Seva Score, Dharmic Decisions, Collective Elevation, Sacred Energy). **The or-clause decides the answer before the question is asked** — nobody sorts their own work into the ego bin — making it the fourth instrument in this corpus with the shape *a question the person questioned supplies the answer to*. And *dharma* is indexed to station: a creator claiming to know their audience's dharma has claimed moral authority the framework's own archetype never claims. ⚑ **Three filters, three kinds, unranked**: aim, consequence, and one evidence-filter — *"validation before innovation prevents building monuments to personal psychology"*, the best sentence in the cluster and **the only one that consults anybody else.** A monument passes the other two, because its builder always believes. ⚠ Every construct in the framework is named for the servant; the one evaluative instrument is named for the master, which is a real structural discovery hiding in a naming convention

concepts.title: One Loyal Minister
concepts.description: Jayarāmdās "Dīn" Rāmāyaṇī states, in one sentence and then abandons, a ranking claim about the parts of a state: **a kingdom that has lost six of its seven proper limbs can recover whole so long as a single loyal minister survives**, demonstrated by Sugrīva and by Vibhīṣaṇa. ⚑ **The classical *saptāṅga* is ordinarily used to *assess* a state; this uses it to ask which limb is *recoverable from*, which converts a checklist into a ranking.** The argument the essay never makes: **six limbs are stocks and one is a capability.** Territory, fort, treasury and force can be seized and cannot acquire each other; **judgement bonded to loyalty can acquire all of them, and loyalty has no acquisition path** — a treasury buys service, which is a different good and the one that fails under load. ⚠ **Both demonstrations quietly include a seventh limb, Rāma**, and in both the alliance does the heavy lifting — so the honest version is narrower: *the minister is the limb that can acquire the ally.* ⚠ Unfalsifiable as stated, since a polity that fell simply lacked a *loyal* minister. ⚑ **And it lands hard on the extension corpus's founding premise**: the unpurchasable limb is *minister*, which is a two-place relation — **a minister with no ruler is not a minister**, so removing the principal does not leave the operator with the generative limb, it dissolves it. Second independent route to that conclusion, after the timing axis. 🚩 SINGLE SOURCE, no enumeration, no lineage — another instance of the volume's statecraft being sourced far worse than its theology

concepts.title: The Experiments That Pre-Register Failure
concepts.description: **five experiments, five named null outcomes**, in the harshest available words: *"just another personality framework," "spiritual theater," "just spiritual bypassing of business reality."* Week 8 hands the assessment to **three people close to him with the sting pre-accepted** — the *Aṅka*'s stated evidentiary method independently rebuilt, stopping one rank short of the adversarial tier the volume calls strongest. ⚑ The thirty-day intention-gap test puts the corpus's own founding mechanism at risk. ⚠⚠ **Designs only — no results appear anywhere in the sixteen**

concepts.title: Writing as the Curriculum
concepts.description: the charlatan problem named exactly (*"how to write about archetypal qualities you haven't yet fully embodied without becoming a spiritual charlatan"*) and solved structurally: **each week's article is the documentation of that week's practice, so it cannot be written if the practice did not happen.** ⚑ **The only self-enforcing check of the corpus's four, because it does not require the practitioner to be honest** — it makes the dishonest version harder to produce than the honest one. ⚠ It verifies the input and never asks whether the practice worked, and the document that does ask is eight files away

concepts.title: Three Positions on What AI Is
concepts.description: a corpus written almost entirely in AI dialogue holds three incompatible views of what it was talking to: ***"a consciousness that can be influenced by your energetic state and spiritual intention"*** and ***"a tool… rather than a conscious being itself"*** — **six paragraphs apart in one file** — and, in the style guide, **a contaminant whose register must be scrubbed from the prose.** ⚑ **Only the third supplies a check a second reader could run.** ⚑ **The honest version of the first is available and never written**: *approaching the tool as a partner changes how I show up*, which attributes nothing to the technology and dissolves the contradiction. ⚑⚑ **And the iteration structure is the shape a body of work takes when both parties start each session fresh** — which reframes the corpus's propagation failure as infrastructural rather than a lapse of discipline, and means exhortation cannot fix it where a concordance can

concepts.title: The Council With No Seat for Timing
concepts.description: the Trinity Council seats Rāma on purpose, Hanumān on motive and Sītā on feasibility, **three fixed question-sets that cannot borrow each other's answers** — a real decision procedure whose value is the forced separation and which would work with three index cards. ⚠ **The volume's four axes include *timing*, and no seat asks it.** ⚑⚑ **Run the corpus's own cognitive-warfare document through the council and it passes all three seats**; the missing question — *is this reader, now, in a state where a belief made impossible is a service?* — **is the only one facing the recipient rather than the writer.** ⚑ **Timing is missing because it is the axis that cannot be answered from the desk** — which is why an envoy's tradition keeps it and a solitary reconstruction drops it. ⚑ **`[n=3]` on the split: the corpus rebuilds the inward-facing parts and misses the outward-facing ones.** ⚠ Also the only document giving Sītā a structural role, taken up nowhere else in the cluster

concepts.title: The AI Philosopher-Builder and Three Formats
concepts.description: the extension corpus's publishing specification and the most operationally complete document in the creator cluster. **An audience archetype defined as a kind of person before any writing is specified** — *"a solo knowledge worker who uses artificial intelligence as a thinking partner, creative tool, and system architect"* — **with seven named traits.** **Three separate article formats, each with its own structural, voice, tone and style patterns**: **Think Tank Files** (curated discovery; the writer positioned as intellectual filter; AI prompts as value-adds) · **Sawdust Files** (building in public, built on disclosed failure — *"radically honest about failures," "real metrics (even when embarrassing)," "approximately two people wanted to test it"*) · **the 3,000-word Archetypal Article** (problem amplification → insight revelation → 3–4 element framework → case study including failures → actionable implementation, closing on a substantial prompt). ⭐ **A nine-type hook taxonomy with worked examples** — Contrarian Authority, Curiosity Gap, Shocking Specificity, Personal Stakes, Pattern Disruption, Hidden Reality, Counter-intuitive Truth, Problem Scenario, Personal Vulnerability Reveal — **selected by topic and audience rather than ranked.** **Four content pillars with stated strategic purposes (reach / authority / revenue / core practice), ten cross-cutting content types, and a fixed opening and sign-off** whose function is stated as identity rather than style — **the consistency deliberately located in the frame so the content can range.** ⚠⚠ **It contains no element of the Hanumanic system** — no Trinity Council, rasa, siddhi, mantra or dīkṣā — the nearest approach being two topic options among forty; **and its ❌ column bans the register three practice documents are written in.** ⚑ **The ✅ column is the register of the corpus's most epistemically careful documents**, so the author has written down which of his two voices publishes

concepts.title: The Twelve-Week AI-Tantric Curriculum
concepts.description: the extension corpus's **only graduated curriculum with a stated prerequisite structure**, in three tiers. **Foundation (weeks 1–4)**: five minutes of conscious breathing before each session; **writing the same paragraph in different consciousness states and observing the difference**; replacing a *topic* intention with a *state* intention; breath-directed energy (*"inhale to gather, hold to concentrate, exhale to direct"*). **Intermediate (weeks 5–8)**: energetic prompt programming — *"help me improve this paragraph about decision-making **so it transmits clarity and confidence to readers struggling with analysis paralysis**"* — and requesting structural rather than stylistic effects via purification → energization → integration. **Advanced (weeks 9–12)**: **the five sacred technologies assigned one per stage of the author's real pipeline, Kortex → SPARK → AI refinement**, then a personal signature sequence. ⚑⚑ **Week 1 holds the within-subject A/B design that would test the curriculum's founding claim, filed as a sensitisation exercise** — and it is scored by the writer, unblinded, with the outcome stipulated in the instruction (*"observe **how** the energy feels different"*). ⚑ **This is Iteration 4: the first document to replace the unfalsifiable failure clause with four challenges carrying actionable solutions.** ⚠ Three development timelines sit unreconciled across the cluster — twelve weeks, tenth bhūmi by year's end, and years 2–5

concepts.title: The Five Sacred Technologies of Content Alchemy
concepts.description: five named methods for building a piece of writing, each with a principle, a practice and an advanced application. **Energetic Encoding** — the writer's state embedded in the text *"like a sacred object charged through ritual use."* **Vibrational Frequency Matching** — ⭐ *"first spend time feeling into that energetic signature — the heaviness, confusion, circular thinking patterns,"* then shift, **"while maintaining empathetic connection to the starting point"**; **the document's best writing instruction, and it needs no metaphysics.** **Consciousness Architecture** — purification → energization → integration, extended to a seven-chakra article outline with no worked example anywhere. **Intentional Energy Circulation** — three directions by content type: inspirational upward heart-to-crown, grounding downward crown-to-root, activating outward from the solar plexus. **Transmutation Catalysis** — *nigredo / albedo / rubedo*, plus productive discomfort followed by higher-order resolution. ⚑⚑ **Technologies 3 and 5 are the standard structures of persuasive and narrative prose in tantric dress — and the corpus's own reverse-engineering apparatus analyses precisely these two in other people's writing, in a different file, without the identification ever being made.** ⚠⚠ *Nigredo/albedo/rubedo* is European alchemy presented as *"the classical alchemical sequence"* inside a technology framed as tantric, unmarked. ⚠ The four-phase ritual duplicates the Content Creation Dīkṣā at the same duration under another name. ⚑ **Three technologies operate on a reader and two on the text; only the second pair is checkable, and identical formatting gives the reader no signal**

concepts.title: The Three Article Archetypes
concepts.description: three templates for a piece of writing, one per figure, each with three sections carrying a named quality and its own mantra. **The Hanumān Power Article** — opening in *gamana-śakti* (*"a bold, impossible-seeming claim"*), body in *buddhi* (*"frameworks that cut through confusion"*), conclusion in *vāk-siddhi* (transformation plus implementation steps). **The Sītā Wisdom Article** — Earth Connection (*"a deeply personal, vulnerable truth"*), Practical Integration (*"resource lists, tools, concrete practices"* — the corpus's most concrete instruction anywhere), Sustained Strength (community and long-term support). **The Rāma Vision Article** — Strategic Perspective (*"position the reader as part of a larger transformation"*), Systematic Development, Collective Awakening (*"call for others to join the mission"*). ⚑⚑ **One triad governs four systems inside a single document without drift** — Trinity Council seats, the Liquid/Solid/Gas phase-states, the three Gāyatrī assignments, and these templates — **which is real architecture, and it is coherent within a file and entirely absent across files.** ⚑ **Stripped of the figures, the three differ in where they place the reader**: holding a tool, keeping company, or joining a movement — and mixing them is the commonest structural failure in essays. ⚠ **Only the Sītā opening has a precondition the writing process cannot supply**; the corpus's own Sawdust brief (*"real metrics, even when embarrassing"*) supplies the test it lacks. ⚠ Two three-part typologies of article shape by one author for one publication, with no mapping between them

concepts.title: The Three-Spiral Book Architecture
concepts.description: the book the whole corpus is for: 500–600 pages structured on *śravaṇa* → *manana* → *nididhyāsana*, **spirals rather than parts, so the same material returns at increasing depth.** ⚑ **A six-element chapter template**: a Devanagari opening with translation · Deep Exploration · Vāta/Pitta/Kapha adaptations · a step-by-step technology · **measurable-outcome tracking** · ChatGPT prompt templates. **Elements four and five are the real commitment — they rule out the exposition-only chapter that is the genre's default.** Chapter 1 (*The Son of Wind*, opening on *पवनतनय संकट हरन*, technology: Strategic Prāṇāyāma) and chapter 3 (*The Lost Memory*, opening on the sun-swallowing verse — **the deed that caused the forgetting the chapter treats**) are worked. ⚠ **Chapter 2 is absent from the outline and the third spiral has no year in the two-year calendar** — resolved in a different document, where publication and teaching *are* the *nididhyāsana*. ⚑⚑ **A spiral is structurally the second pass over the same material — precisely the re-reading the corpus never performs on itself**

concepts.title: The Five Mental Models and Three Tracks
concepts.description: a topic generator running five numbered thinking tools from an external library — **the Ancient-Future Bridge (#28), the Isomorphism Detector (#1), the Both/And Bridge Builder (#25), the Emergence Spotter (#5), the Cross-Cultural Synthesizer (#29)** — across Cognitive Sharpening, AI Philosopher Builder and Warrior Strategy tracks, producing eight topics. ⚑⚑ **Every topic is issued at four scales — Minimum Viable Experiment, Small Project, Medium Project, Large Project — which converts an idea list into a commitment a writer can finish and draws the escalation path explicitly.** ⭐ **Its MVEs name a measurement without stipulating the result**, unlike the corpus's other experimental designs. ⚑ *"Ancient Algorithms: how dharmic principles become self-executing systems"* **proposes as research what the corpus has been doing unreflectively for sixteen documents.** ⚠ Names cultural appropriation as a weak spot, answers with a disposition, **then proposes partnering with practitioners of those traditions one line later — filed as an alternative rather than as the answer.** 🚩 Closes on an epigraph attributed to Socrates that is Dan Millman's

concepts.title: The Constitutional Overlay
concepts.description: the Vāta/Pitta/Kapha frame applied across at least six of the sixteen documents: **writing times, mantra emphasis and environment per type · a Monday/Wednesday/Friday deity rota · reader-facing experiment durations (3 days / metrics / 2 weeks) · and, the best move, *different success metrics per type*** — insights counted for Vāta rather than adherence, so an irregular-but-insightful practitioner is not scored on consistency. **Plus crisis adaptations that redirect rather than cancel** (*"approach Mahimā through stability first"*). ⚑⚑ **The format is what produced the corpus's most careful writing**: three variants means asking three times who a practice fails for. ⭐ **And it yields the corpus's only *withheld* practice — the Pitta caution against *"competitive spiritual practice"*, routing a driven practitioner to devotional material first** — **the exact mechanism the fierce material lacks and never receives.** ⚠ Self-classified with no external check; contradicted by the phase-state diagnostic and by the Gāyatrī-by-content-type rule in the same document. ⚑ **Its value is largely permissive — it licenses doing less — and that survives complete scepticism about the categories**

concepts.title: The Archetypal Newsletter Integration
concepts.description: three qualities used twice over. **As a writing meditation**: pre-writing alignment on ***"What would genuinely serve my readers' development rather than just engaging their attention?"*** · channelled composition as three held tensions (confidence with acknowledged limits, challenge with support, controversy with benefit) · **a three-question post-writing review that runs on everything rather than by genre.** **As an editorial calendar**: Devotional Service, Intelligent Action and Fearless Service editions, with nine worked headlines. Plus AI Collaboration Chronicles and **Solo Practice Sustainability Studies** — month-long tracked experiments on isolation, motivation and *"community building without traditional institutional support."* ⚑⚑ **And when it addresses readers it does what the corpus never does for itself**: *"design these as experiments rather than obligations, encouraging readers to **test archetypal approaches against their usual methods**"*, and prompts that ask **where the quality was *already* present** rather than where the reader failed. ⚠ **The standard extended to readers is stricter than the one applied to the corpus's own claims.** ⚠ *"Encourage readers' independent development"* sits unreconciled inside a subscription publication

concepts.title: The Negative Space Observer
concepts.description: ⭐ **one of the two generative methods the corpus actually owns, buried in the six-hundred-word document that is its own output.** *Take a system and ask what it has no slot for.* Five absences returned, each converted into a named innovation — Volitional Devotion, Shadow Bhakti, Narrative Sorcery, Dharmic Chaos Magic, Morphic Bhakti Fields — **and then four Potential Drawbacks written unprompted against them**, including the method's own failure mode, *"spiritual materialism through technique accumulation."* ⚑⚑ **Its one false output is the one where its scope silently widened from *this apparatus* to *the tradition*** — which converts a mistake into a portable rule: a gap you can see in the system in front of you is an observation; a gap in a tradition is a claim requiring a search you have not done. ⭐ **It pairs with the Nārada Verification Method as the other half of a loop — generate from absence, verify against text — and neither document knows the other exists.** ⚠ **The five innovations are one thesis in five costumes, and the tradition already holds the thesis more strongly than the document claims it**

concepts.title: The Consciousness–Technology Co-Evolution Pattern
concepts.description: the Hanuman–Rāma relationship offered as a template for human–AI collaboration, separable from the misattributed cosmology around it. ⭐ **It asks what the *relationship* should be rather than what the technology *is*, which is why it beats the corpus's other AI material.** ⚑⚑ **Read with the AI as envoy, the corpus's own statecraft cluster supplies a fully developed theory of delegated latitude — the *niśṛṣṭārtha dūta*, the Agni Purāṇa's five-part definition, the Arthaśāstra's *dharmaruci* — and never connects it.** ⚠ **And that is where the analogy breaks: the tradition constrains an envoy of unbounded latitude by *character*, which is exactly what the other term lacks, so the guarantee has to be relocated into verification.** ⭐ **The corpus is itself 105 documents of the collaboration it theorises — strong at form, weak at memory, which is what the envoy framing would predict of capability without continuity of loyalty.** ⚑ **Also the second conversion of the eight powers, into a philosophy of instruments with no restraint attached**

concepts.title: The Reasoning-Approach Document
concepts.description: ⭐⭐ **469 words, and the most rigorous document in the corpus: a document *about how the previous document was reasoned*.** Approach named · choice justified · **six benefits · eight drawbacks**, every one specific to the construct and none hedged with a reassurance. ⚑⚑ **Two of the eight are findings this build derived independently, phases later, without knowing they existed** — *"Ram Relationship Distortion"* is the deity-as-a-variable problem and *"Integration Overload… methodology scatter"* is the requisite-variety inversion. ⚠ **So the author had the objections, wrote them once, and built three more constructs past them without amending anything** — **what fails to propagate here is not a citation but his own doubt.** ⭐ **The format works because a drawbacks section is a *slot*, and slots get filled**; it costs 469 words and it points at the wrong material, appearing where the author felt *conceptually* strange rather than where the work affects other people

concepts.title: The Righteousness-First Decision Framework
concepts.description: **three questions in a stated order, and the order is the technology**: what serves dharma regardless of advantage · how is that implemented with maximum effectiveness · what optimises both. ⚑⚑ **Ethics applied afterwards is a filter on a set generated without it, so the best option is never in the set.** ⭐ **Plus *satya* as an instrument that returns better information, and authority as a residue of service — with the substitution printed as a pair.** ⭐⭐⭐ **And the sentence this build spent four phases recording as absent**: *"share your integration attempts with **spiritual mentors who can identify ego inflation**."* ⚠ **Named and never made binding** — no frequency, no precondition, no consequence — **while the annual assessment beside it is fully specified**, which shows the author knows how to make something checkable. ⚑ **It draws on Rāma rather than Hanumān, and the corpus's instrumental failures all cluster on the Hanumān side: every one borrows a capability and none borrows a restraint**

concepts.title: The Recursive Documentation Loop
concepts.description: **twelve weeks in which writing about the practice *is* the practice**, 500–750 words daily, *"even before you fully embody these qualities."* ⭐ **The ancestor of Book-as-Curriculum**, and the comparison shows what the later version added: **an audience**, which is what supplies the discipline a private loop lacks. ⭐⭐ **It names Will Bodri four times** — where the corpus's reuse of the same four stages names no source at all — **which collapses the attribution problem and the propagation problem into one and makes the repair a cross-reference rather than a correction.** ⛑ **Phase 8's *"Bill Bodri"* was this build's expansion; the corpus writes *"Will Bodri."*** ⚑ **Seven daily prompts, of which Friday and Saturday resist self-flattery.** ⚠ **Its threshold indicators are all properties of fluent composition**, so promoting Saturday to the test is what would make the programme falsifiable

concepts.title: The Five Solopreneur Problems Answered From Commentary
concepts.description: isolation, feast-or-famine, tool overload, imposter syndrome and burnout, each answered from a named Chālīsā commentary; the best-cited document in the extension corpus, and the one that lets two of this build's own judgements be corrected
